chapter: Ch 10: Accounting Standards for Consolidated Financial Statements
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Introduction, Scope and Objective of AS 23
explain: AS 23 came into effect for accounting periods starting on or after April 1, 2002.
It lays down principles for recognizing investments in associates in Consolidated Financial Statements (CFS).
In an investor's Separate Financial Statements (SFS), AS 13 is followed for investment in associates.
Compliance with AS 23 is compulsory for companies that prepare CFS under AS 21.
topics.example: If Company A holds a 30% stake in Company B, it uses AS 13 in its own separate balance sheet, but applies AS 23 when preparing its group consolidated financial statements.
remember: AS 23 applies only in Consolidated Financial Statements (CFS), whereas AS 13 applies in Separate Financial Statements (SFS).
mistakes: Applying AS 23 in separate financial statements of the investor instead of AS 13.

quiz.q: Which accounting standard applies to investments in associates in an investor's Separate Financial Statements?
quiz.why: AS 13 governs investments in separate financial statements, while AS 23 applies to consolidated financial statements.

quiz.q: When did AS 23 come into effect?
quiz.why: AS 23 became effective for accounting periods commencing on or after April 1, 2002.

topics.title: Key Definitions & Presumption of Significant Influence
explain: An associate is an enterprise in which the investor has significant influence, but is neither a subsidiary nor a joint venture.
Significant influence is the power to participate in financial and operating policy decisions, but not control over them.
If an investor holds directly or indirectly 20% or more of voting power, significant influence is presumed to exist.
The Equity Method records investment initially at cost and adjusts carrying amount for post-acquisition changes in net assets.

flow.title: Identifying an Associate
steps: Check for Control or Joint Venture

topics.example: Company A buys 25% of voting shares in Company B without holding majority board seats. Company B is classified as an associate of Company A.
remember: 20% or more voting power creates a presumption of significant influence unless proved otherwise.
mistakes: Treating a subsidiary or a joint venture as an associate.

quiz.q: What is the minimum voting power presumed to give significant influence under AS 23?
quiz.why: Holding 20% or more of voting power creates a statutory presumption of significant influence.

quiz.q: An associate enterprise under AS 23 CANNOT be a:
quiz.why: By definition, an associate is neither a subsidiary nor a joint venture of the investor.

topics.title: Indicators of Significant Influence & Concept of Control
explain: Significant influence can exist with less than 20% voting power if evidenced by practical indicators.
Indicators include board representation, policy participation, material inter-company transactions, interchange of managerial staff, or provision of technical info.
Control exists if the parent holds >50% voting power or controls the composition of the board of directors.
Trusts like Gratuity or PF trusts controlled without economic benefit objectives are excluded from consolidated financial statements.
topics.example: Company X owns only 15% of Company Y, but holds a board seat and supplies essential technical secrets. Significant influence exists.
remember: Control requires over 50% voting power or board composition control; trusts without economic benefit are excluded from CFS.
mistakes: Including employee welfare trusts (like PF trusts) in CFS just because the company controls their board composition.

quiz.q: Which of the following demonstrates significant influence even if shareholding is under 20%?
quiz.why: Interchange of managerial personnel is a recognized indicator of significant influence under AS 23.

quiz.q: Why are controlling trusts such as Gratuity and PF trusts excluded from Consolidated Financial Statements?
o: The objective is not obtaining economic benefit
They are audited under separate laws
quiz.why: AS 23 excludes entities where control is not exercised to obtain economic benefits from their activities.

topics.title: Working of the Equity Method
explain: Investment is initially recorded at cost in the Consolidated Financial Statements.
Goodwill or Capital Reserve is identified at acquisition (Cost minus Investor's share of Net Assets).
Goodwill/Capital Reserve is included in the carrying amount but disclosed separately.
Post-acquisition profit share increases the carrying amount, while dividends received reduce it.
Consolidated P&L reflects the investor's share of the investee's operating results.

flow.title: Equity Method Calculation Process
steps: Report Final Carrying Amount in CFS

topics.example: A Ltd. buys 45% of B Ltd. for Rs. 15,00,000 when B Ltd.'s net assets are Rs. 16,00,000. Share of net assets is Rs. 7,20,000, creating Goodwill of Rs. 7,80,000. Profit share adds to cost, and dividends reduce cost.
remember: Dividends received from an associate reduce the carrying amount of investment in CFS under the equity method.
mistakes: Adding dividend received to the carrying amount of investment instead of deducting it.

quiz.q: Under the Equity Method in CFS, how do dividends received from an associate affect the investment account?
quiz.why: Distributions received from an investee reduce the carrying amount of the investment under the equity method.

quiz.q: How is Goodwill arising on acquisition of an associate presented in CFS?
o: Shown as a separate asset line item
Included in investment carrying amount and disclosed separately
quiz.why: Goodwill/Capital Reserve is included in the carrying amount of investment in associate but disclosed separately.

topics.title: Exceptions & Discontinuation of Equity Method
explain: Equity method is NOT followed if investment is acquired and held temporarily for near-future disposal.
It is also NOT followed if associate operates under severe long-term restrictions impairing fund transfers.
In these exceptional cases, the investment is accounted for under AS 13.
Discontinue equity method when significant influence ceases or severe restrictions apply.
Carrying amount at the discontinuation date is treated as cost thereafter under AS 13.

flow.title: Selecting Accounting Standard for Associate Investment
steps: If Neither Exists, Use AS 23 Equity Method

topics.example: Company A buys a 30% stake in Company B explicitly to sell it within 3 months. Company A accounts for it under AS 13 instead of AS 23 equity method.
remember: On discontinuation of equity method, carrying amount on that date becomes cost under AS 13.
mistakes: Continuing the equity method when an associate is subjected to severe long-term restrictions on dividend transfers.

quiz.q: In which case is the Equity Method NOT applied to an associate?
o: Investment is acquired for temporary disposal in near future
Associate earns profit during the year
quiz.why: Investments acquired and held exclusively for near-future disposal are accounted under AS 13.

quiz.q: When equity method is discontinued, what value becomes the cost under AS 13 going forward?
quiz.why: The carrying amount of the investment at the date of discontinuation is regarded as cost under AS 13.

topics.title: Special Accounting Rules: Step Acquisition, Losses & Transactions
explain: Step Acquisition: If stake is acquired in stages, Goodwill/Capital Reserve is calculated at each step.
Inter-company Transactions: Unrealized profits on transactions are eliminated to the extent of investor's share.
Loss Limit: Share of losses cannot reduce investment carrying amount below zero unless investor has guaranteed obligations.
Reporting Dates: Gap between reporting dates of investor and associate cannot exceed 6 months.
Uniform Policies: Financial statements must be prepared using uniform accounting policies for like transactions.

flow.title: Handling Associate Loss Allocation
steps: Resume Profits Only After Past Unrecognized Losses Cleared

topics.example: If carrying amount of associate investment is Rs. 1,00,000 and current loss share is Rs. 2,00,000, write down investment to Nil and stop recognizing the excess Rs. 1,00,000 loss.
remember: Difference between reporting dates of investor and associate should not be more than 6 months.
mistakes: Showing a negative investment carrying amount when the investor has no legal commitment to cover associate liabilities.

quiz.q: What is the maximum allowed difference between reporting dates of investor and associate under AS 23?
quiz.why: AS 23 mandates that the difference between reporting dates should not be more than 6 months.

quiz.q: What happens when an investor's share of losses exceeds the carrying amount of investment in an associate?
o: Loss recognition stops at zero value
quiz.why: Investor discontinues recognizing further losses once carrying amount reaches nil, unless obligations are incurred.

topics.title: Disclosure Requirements & Relevant Explanations
explain: Disclose list of associates, proportion of ownership interest, and voting power (if different).
Investments in associates must be classified as long-term investments in Consolidated Balance Sheet.
Proposed Dividend: Investor's share of operating results is computed WITHOUT considering proposed dividends.
Potential Equity Shares: Convertible instruments held are NOT taken into account for determining voting power.

flow.title: Evaluating Voting Power and Dividend Disclosures
steps: Exclude Potential Shares from Voting Power
Calculate Profit Share Without Proposed Dividend
Classify as Long-Term Investment in CFS

topics.example: Company A holds convertible debentures that could yield 10% shares in Company B later. These potential shares are ignored when determining Company A's present voting power in Company B.
remember: Proposed dividends declared after reporting period are excluded when calculating investor's share of associate results.
mistakes: Including potential equity shares to determine present voting power of an investor.

quiz.q: How are potential equity shares treated when determining voting power under AS 23?
quiz.why: Potential equity shares held by investor are not taken into account for determining present voting power.

quiz.q: How is proposed dividend of an associate treated while computing investor's share of results?
o: Computed without taking proposed dividend into consideration
quiz.why: Investor's share of results of operations of associate is computed without taking proposed dividend into consideration.
